links.outcome: Readability of chatbot plagiocephaly responses versus recommended thresholds (FKGL, SMOG, Flesch Reading Ease)
links.effect: No model met recommended readability thresholds; FKGL 11.66 to 13.14, SMOG 12.77 to 15.10, Flesch Reading Ease 34.60 to 45.71.
links.quote: None met recommended readability thresholds: Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level ranged from 11.66 to 13.14, Simple Measure of Gobbledygook from 12.77 to 15.10, and Flesch Reading Ease from 34.60 to 45.71.

links.outcome: Source transparency of chatbot responses (JAMA Benchmark Criteria)
links.effect: Median JAMA scores were 1.00 for ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Copilot and 0.00 for Gemini; source transparency was described as limited.
links.quote: Artificial intelligence chatbots provided coherent, relatively complete plagiocephaly information, but quality varied, source transparency was limited, and readability was poor.

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of four commercial LLM chatbots answering consumer health questions on plagiocephaly, assessing quality, transparency, and readability metrics without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment intervention.
